claim_summary: TS-Agent contributes a feedback-driven time-series QA runtime that gathers evidence from raw-series tools, records observations, refines tool use, and verifies answers against required evidence.

claim_evidence.quote: Our framework solves time series tasks through an evidence-driven agentic process: (1) it alternates between thinking, tool execution, and observation in a ReAct-style loop, (2) records intermediate results in an explicit evidence log and corrects the reasoning trace via a self-refinement critic, and (3) enforces a final answer-verification step

modules.name: Adaptive reasoner loop with evidence log
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK no: the loop selects actions across question types without embedding one task family's output requirement or verifier. R3_2_GTS no: the thought/action/observation state and the evidence log accumulate observations of any tool; the log imposes no windows, frequency, units or availability-time semantics. R3_3_GH yes: it manages execution and state; the evidence log only functions together with the loop, so it is merged here.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - not bound to one task objective
R3_2_GTS:no - generic action and observation state, no temporal semantics
R3_3_GH:yes - runtime execution control and state

evidence.quote: At the core of our framework is an iterative LLM reasoner that drives the reasoning process through cycles of thought, action, and observation. Rather than producing a fixed plan upfront, the agent adaptively generates the next reasoning step only after incorporating the structured outcome of the previous step.

Formally, let T = {t1 , . . . , tM } be the set of callable tools, and Lk = {e1 , . . . , eM } be evidence log, i.e., the memory module that records of all accumulated observations produced during reasoning.

modules.name: Raw-series analytical tools
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK no: the library supports summarization, extraction, querying, detection, prediction, and relations across question types. R3_2_GTS yes: its tools operate on raw numerical series and temporal windows, slices, segments, and resampling; the same operators remain useful across task families. R3_3_GH is not reached because temporal data semantics are more specific.
rubric_path: R3_2_GTS:yes - operates on raw series and temporal windows

evidence.quote: To support fine-grained and verifiable reasoning, TS-AGENT is equipped with a library of callable analytical APIs that operate directly on native numeric time series and return structured outputs.

Extract (fext : X × Θ → X ). These tools extract part of the time series for subsequent local analysis, such as selecting channels, slicing a temporal interval, segmenting into subseries, or resampling to a desired granularity.

modules.name: Step-wise self-refinement critic
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK no: it reviews tool use and evidence across question types, rather than imposing one task-family criterion. R3_2_GTS no: it consumes time-series results but does not itself implement windows, chronology, or availability semantics. R3_3_GH yes: it changes later runtime actions through feedback; a TSK critic would require task-specific review rules, while this execution review is shared.

evidence.quote: After the execution of each action, we invoke the same LLM in a critic role to assess the new evidence in the context of the accumulated reasoning trace and the evidence log.

modules.name: Intent-specific answer verification gate
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK yes: the gate checks question-intent predicates and answer schemas, so another task family would require different requirements and verifiers. If it were GTS, it would validate temporal validity independently of task; this gate validates a temporal QA answer's task-specific schema and evidence requirements. R3_2_GTS is not selected because R3_1 matches first.

evidence.quote: Final Answer Verification. When the agent proposes an answer ŷ, we pass it to a quality gate which enforces data-grounding before output.

the gate checks: (i) schema compliance—ŷ matches schema (e.g., belongs to the MCQ option set); and (ii) evidence sufficiency—all required predicates are verified (Gk = ∅) and no contradictions remain.

process_validity.quote: provides feedback about the expected input format, leading the agent to correct its tool usage.

task_performance.quote: We first evaluate TS-AGENT on time series understanding tasks using the TimeSeriesExam benchmark (Cai et al., 2024), which contains 763 multiple-choice questions over five categories: pattern recognition, noise understanding, anomaly detection, similarity analysis, and causality analysis.

changes: dimension: Planning and Workflow -> Planning and Orchestration
layer stays GH (candidate GTS evidence-log rejected, merged back)
reconciliation.reason: The evidence log is generic observation storage that only functions with the thought/action/observation loop, so it stays inside the GH module.

changes: name: Numeric time-series analytical operators -> Raw-series analytical tools
reconciliation.reason: Mechanism and layer unchanged; the temporal function is processing (windowing, slicing, resampling, statistics).

changes: dimension: Control, Verification, and Feedback -> Planning and Orchestration
reconciliation.reason: The paper describes the critic and final answer gate as complementary, distinct mechanisms. The gate is task-specific; the critic is a separate runtime feedback module omitted as a distinct module in the card.

notes: Context-aided forecasting appears only as a benchmark task type (TSandLang); the work is mainly temporal QA. Evaluation reports no temporal-validity (chronology or information-cutoff) evidence: the leakage discussed is knowledge leakage.

items.item: evidence-loop layer GH->GH GTS (evidence-log split as GTS)
items.result: One GH module (loop plus evidence log); no GTS log module
items.reason: The log stores observations from any tool and carries no temporal window, frequency, unit or availability semantics; R3_2 fails, R3_3 holds, and the log only works with the loop.

The gate's intent classes, required predicates and answer schemas (MCQ option sets, anomaly location) embed the output requirement of the question; R3_1 counterfactual requires redesign for another task. The generic critic is the separate GH module.
The paper presents the critic and final gate as complementary mechanisms; critic checks tool suitability, plausibility, sufficiency and redirects actions.
Extract/Detect/Summarize/Predict operators process series; no timestamp, unit or provenance management is contributed.

adjudication.summary: Kept the candidate split of critic and gate, but merged the evidence log back into the GH loop and dropped data_management from the operators. The answer gate stays TSK because its predicates and schemas are question-intent specific.
